name: outw
prose: Static inline helper that writes the 16-bit value data to I/O port port with the x86 outw instruction (value in AX, port in DX via the 'Nd' constraint); returns void and has no C-level side effects other than the port write.
note: cpufunc.h (i386) outw: single asm statement, no checks of port or data.

name: read_eflags
prose: Static inline helper that returns the current EFLAGS register as a u_int, read with pushfl followed by popl into a register.
note: cpufunc.h read_eflags: one asm statement.

name: rdmsr
prose: Static inline helper that executes the privileged rdmsr instruction for model-specific register number msr (in ECX) and returns the 64-bit value from EDX:EAX; if the MSR is not valid or the caller lacks privilege the CPU raises an exception rather than returning.
note: cpufunc.h rdmsr: asm with =A output; the exception behaviour is the hardware's, not coded here.

name: rdmsr32
prose: Static inline helper that executes rdmsr for model-specific register msr and returns only the low 32 bits (EAX); the high half in EDX is discarded (clobbered). Invalid MSRs raise a CPU exception as for rdmsr.
note: cpufunc.h rdmsr32.

name: rdpmc
prose: Static inline helper that executes rdpmc for performance counter number pmc (in ECX) and returns the 64-bit counter value from EDX:EAX.
note: cpufunc.h rdpmc.

name: rdtsc
prose: Static inline helper that executes rdtsc and returns the 64-bit time-stamp counter from EDX:EAX; it does not serialize the instruction stream.
note: cpufunc.h rdtsc: bare rdtsc, no fence.

name: rdtsc_ordered_lfence
prose: Static inline helper that issues lfence and then returns rdtsc(), so the counter read is ordered after earlier loads.
note: cpufunc.h rdtsc_ordered_lfence: lfence(); return (rdtsc()).

name: rdtsc_ordered_mfence
prose: Static inline helper that issues mfence and then returns rdtsc(), so the counter read is ordered after earlier loads and stores.
note: cpufunc.h rdtsc_ordered_mfence: mfence(); return (rdtsc()).

name: rdtscp
prose: Static inline helper that executes rdtscp and returns the 64-bit time-stamp counter from EDX:EAX; the auxiliary value in ECX is discarded (ECX is declared clobbered).
note: cpufunc.h rdtscp.

name: rdtscp_aux
prose: Static inline helper that executes rdtscp, returns the 64-bit time-stamp counter, and stores the auxiliary value from ECX (IA32_TSC_AUX) in *aux; aux must be a valid pointer.
note: cpufunc.h rdtscp_aux: *aux written through the asm ECX output.

name: rdtsc32
prose: Static inline helper that executes rdtsc and returns only the low 32 bits (EAX) of the time-stamp counter; EDX is declared clobbered.
note: cpufunc.h rdtsc32.

name: rdtscp32
prose: Static inline helper that executes rdtscp and returns only the low 32 bits (EAX) of the time-stamp counter; ECX and EDX are declared clobbered, so the auxiliary value is discarded.
note: cpufunc.h rdtscp32.

name: write_eflags
prose: Static inline helper that loads the EFLAGS register with the value ef using pushl followed by popfl; returns void. Flags that the current privilege level cannot change are not changed by popfl.
note: cpufunc.h write_eflags: the privilege note is hardware behaviour of popfl.

name: wrmsr
prose: Static inline helper that executes the privileged wrmsr instruction, writing the 64-bit newval (EDX:EAX) to model-specific register msr (ECX); returns void. An invalid MSR or value makes the CPU raise an exception.
note: cpufunc.h wrmsr.

name: load_cr0
prose: Static inline helper that writes the value data to control register CR0 with a mov instruction (privileged); returns void.
note: cpufunc.h load_cr0: no memory clobber.

name: rcr0
prose: Static inline helper that returns the current value of control register CR0 as a u_int.
note: cpufunc.h rcr0.

name: rcr2
prose: Static inline helper that returns the current value of control register CR2 (the faulting linear address of the last page fault) as a u_int.
note: cpufunc.h rcr2.

name: load_cr3
prose: Static inline helper that writes data to control register CR3 (the page-directory base), which also flushes the non-global TLB entries; the asm declares a memory clobber. Returns void.
note: cpufunc.h load_cr3: TLB flush is a hardware effect of the CR3 write.

name: rcr3
prose: Static inline helper that returns the current value of control register CR3 as a u_int.
note: cpufunc.h rcr3.

name: load_cr4
prose: Static inline helper that writes data to control register CR4 with a mov instruction (privileged); returns void.
note: cpufunc.h load_cr4.

name: rcr4
prose: Static inline helper that returns the current value of control register CR4 as a u_int.
note: cpufunc.h rcr4.

name: rxcr
prose: Static inline helper that executes xgetbv for extended control register number reg (ECX) and returns the 64-bit value assembled as low | (high << 32) from EAX and EDX.
note: cpufunc.h rxcr.

name: load_xcr
prose: Static inline helper that executes xsetbv, writing the 64-bit val (split into low 32 bits in EAX and high 32 bits in EDX) to extended control register reg (ECX); returns void.
note: cpufunc.h load_xcr.

name: invltlb
prose: Static inline helper that flushes the non-global TLB entries by reloading CR3 with its current value: load_cr3(rcr3()).
note: cpufunc.h invltlb.

name: invlpg
prose: Static inline helper that invalidates the TLB entry for the page containing linear address addr with the invlpg instruction (memory clobber); returns void.
note: cpufunc.h invlpg.

name: rfs
prose: Static inline helper that returns the current value of the FS segment selector as a u_short.
note: cpufunc.h rfs.

name: rgdt
prose: Static inline helper that returns the contents of the global descriptor table register as a uint64_t, stored with the sgdt instruction into a local 64-bit variable.
note: cpufunc.h rgdt: sgdt writes a 6-byte descriptor into the 8-byte local; the upper 2 bytes of the result are not set by the instruction.

name: ATOMIC_CMPSET(int, "r")
prose: Generated function atomic_cmpset_int(volatile u_int *dst, u_int expect, u_int src), produced by the ATOMIC_CMPSET macro for TYPE int with the "r" constraint. It executes lock cmpxchg: if *dst equals expect it atomically stores src into *dst; the zero flag is captured with sete, and the function returns 1 if the exchange happened and 0 if *dst did not equal expect (in which case *dst is left unchanged). The asm has a memory clobber, so it also acts as a compiler barrier, and the locked instruction is a full hardware barrier. It does not report the value it saw on failure.
note: atomic.h:137-170 (ATOMIC_CMPSET macro) instantiated at 174 for int. Returns the u_char res as int.

name: ATOMIC_CMPSET(int, "r")
prose: Generated function atomic_fcmpset_int(volatile u_int *dst, u_int *expect, u_int src), produced by the ATOMIC_CMPSET macro for TYPE int. It executes lock cmpxchg with the expected value taken from *expect: if *dst equals *expect it atomically stores src into *dst and returns 1. If they differ, it returns 0, leaves *dst unchanged and (because *expect is the in/out EAX operand) writes the value found in *dst back into *expect, so a retry loop can use it. The asm has a memory clobber and the locked instruction is a full barrier.
note: atomic.h:155-169 (fcmpset half of the ATOMIC_CMPSET macro, instantiated at 174 for int).

name: ATOMIC_LOADSTORE(int)
prose: Generated function atomic_load_acq_int(const volatile u_int *p), produced by ATOMIC_LOAD(TYPE) inside ATOMIC_LOADSTORE(int). It reads *p into a local with a plain load, then issues a compiler barrier (__compiler_membar) and returns the value. On i386 no fence instruction is emitted; the acquire ordering relies on x86's load ordering plus the compiler barrier.
note: atomic.h:250-259 (ATOMIC_LOAD macro) instantiated through ATOMIC_LOADSTORE(int) at 599-603. The ATOMIC_LOADSTORE invocation also generates atomic_store_rel_int, which this item does not describe.

name: xl_setmode
prose: Selects the transceiver and duplex for a 3Com xl adapter; static void. Precondition: the softc lock is held (XL_LOCK_ASSERT). It reads the media status register (register window 4) and the internal config register (window 3). Then, for each media option the card reports in sc->xl_media, if the requested media subtype matches: 10baseT (XL_MEDIAOPT_BT, IFM_10_T) sets xl_xcvr to 10BT, rewrites the connector bits of icfg and sets the link-beat and jabber-guard bits and clears SQE enable; 100baseFX (XL_MEDIAOPT_BFX, IFM_100_FX) sets xl_xcvr to 100BFX, the connector bits, sets link-beat and clears SQE enable; AUI (IFM_10_5) or 10baseFL (IFM_10_FL) with XL_MEDIAOPT_AUI or 10FL set xl_xcvr to AUI, the connector bits, clear link-beat and jabber-guard and set mediastat |= ~XL_MEDIASTAT_SQEENB (an OR with the complement, which sets every bit except SQE enable); 10base2 (XL_MEDIAOPT_BNC, IFM_10_2) sets xl_xcvr to COAX, the connector bits and clears link-beat, jabber-guard and SQE enable (its message string is 'AUI port'). The code has no branches for 10baseT4, MII or 100baseTX, and when nothing matches the message string stays empty (it does not say 'unknown'). It then writes the MAC duplex bit through window 3: set for full duplex or 100baseFX, cleared otherwise; issues XL_CMD_COAX_START for 10base2 and XL_CMD_COAX_STOP otherwise; writes icfg to the internal config register and mediastat to the media status register (window 4), waits 800 us, selects window 7 and prints 'selecting <media>, <full|half> duplex' with the chosen strings.
note: if_xl.c:737-830 (packet name was elided; the real function is xl_setmode). Reviewer round 17 wrong on 'unknown' and BT4/MII/BTX: there is no such handling (750-803), and a no-match leaves pmsg as the empty string it was initialized to (741).

name: gdb_trap
prose: Command loop of the GDB remote stub once the kernel debugger has stopped on a trap; returns 1 when the target should resume or the connection ended, and 0 when the packet loop ends. It saves the current kdb jump buffer with kdb_jmpbuf(jb); if a longjmp back to this setjmp happens (an error in the receive path) it sets gdb_listening to 0, restores the saved jump buffer and returns 1. It clears gdb_listening, sends the stop reply with the signal for (type, code) and records the stop reason, then reads packets while gdb_rx_begin() returns 0. '?' replies with the signal; 'c' and 'C' (the latter only when the signal and ';' parse) set the PC register when an address was given, set gdb_listening to 1 and return 1; 's' and 'S' do the same for single stepping and return 1; 'D' replies OK, calls gdb_handle_detach and returns 1; 'k' calls gdb_handle_detach and returns 1; 'g' and 'p' return register values; 'G' and 'P' write registers (EINVAL for a bad format, OK otherwise); 'H' selects a thread (EINVAL for a bad id, ENOENT when not found, OK otherwise); 'm' reads memory (EINVAL for a bad command, EIO when the read fails); 'M' writes memory (EINVAL for a bad command, EIO when the write fails); 'q' answers queries or an empty reply when the CPU-specific query does not handle it; 'Q' handles StartNoAckMode (OK or empty reply depending on a feature flag) and otherwise an empty reply; 'T' replies OK if the thread exists and ENOENT otherwise (EINVAL for a bad id); 'z' and 'Z' remove and insert watchpoints; end of input and unknown commands get an empty reply. When gdb_rx_begin() returns non-zero it restores the saved jump buffer (kdb_jmpbuf(prev_jb)) and returns 0.
note: gdb_main.c:724-992 (packet name 'unnamed enclosing function: GDB stub command loop' is gdb_trap; fixed instead of dropped). Returns 736, 779, 791, 796, 847, 948, 960, 992. PARTLY READ: 'q' (900-922), 'Q' (923-938) and 'z'/'Z' (974-980) handlers via control-flow lines only; the stop-reply format at 747-752 not read in detail.

name: pax_enforce_tpe
prose: Checks Trusted Path Execution for a program being executed; returns 0 or an errno. It returns EDOOFUS if td, vn or path is NULL. It returns 0 if TPE is disabled in the thread's prison or _pax_tpe_active says TPE does not apply to the thread (exempt flag, or the group test with tpe_all, tpe_gid and tpe_negate). It finds the last '/' in path: EDOOFUS if there is none, and 0 if the slash is the last character (strlen of the part from the slash is below 2, i.e. empty file name). It copies the text before the last slash into parent_path, locks vn shared (the VOP_LOCK error is returned) and reads its attributes: a VOP_GETATTR error is returned with vn still locked; otherwise vn is unlocked and the attributes are checked with _pax_tpe_vap(..., S_IWGRP | S_IWOTH), whose EPERM (root-owned and user-owned rules, owner-write bit for non-root owners, group/other write bits) is returned. It then looks up the parent directory with namei (LOOKUP, FOLLOW | LOCKLEAF), returning its error, gets the parent's attributes and applies the same check, unlocks the parent vnode and frees the path buffer, and returns the error of that check (0 when all pass). after parent_path is allocated, every return path frees it.
note: hbsd_grsec_tpe.c:248-328 (packet name 'unnamed TPE path check' is pax_enforce_tpe). Reviewer round 17 right: the 'shorter than 2 characters' case (273-274) means only a trailing slash (strlen 1) returns 0. Returns 257, 262, 266, 271, 274, 284, 291, 299, 309, 327. On the namei error path NDFREE_PNBUF is called, 308.

name: pax_segvguard_segfault
prose: Records a segmentation fault of the process's executable for the segvguard feature; returns 0 or EFAULT. It returns 0 at once if segvguard is not active for the process. It returns EFAULT if td->td_proc->p_textvp is NULL. Otherwise it takes the current uptime, looks the vnode up in the segvguard table (pax_segvguard_lookup, which fills a vattr with VOP_GETATTR and may fail, returning NULL, in which case the vattr is only partly filled), and: if there is no entry it calls pax_segvguard_add(td, v, sbt, &vap), whose result is ignored (the allocation uses M_NOWAIT and can fail, in which case no entry is inserted); if an entry exists and both its expiry and its suspension deadline are in the past it logs, resets the crash count to 1, sets a new expiry and clears the suspension, and returns 0 at that point; otherwise it increments the crash count and, when it reaches pax_segvguard_maxcrashes, logs, sets the suspension deadline, zeroes the crash count and clears the expiry. It returns 0. The hash-bucket lock is taken and released inside the lookup and add helpers, not here.
note: hbsd_pax_segvguard.c:461-513. Reviewer original right (inactive process returns 0, 469-470); round 15 right (pax_segvguard_add can return NULL, 373-376, and its result is ignored at 487). Returns 470, 474, 496, 512.

name: acpi_sleep_machdep
prose: Machine-dependent part of entering an ACPI sleep state on i386; returns -1, 0 or 1. It returns -1 immediately when sc->acpi_wakeaddr is 0 (no wake memory could be allocated). With SMP it prepares the set of other CPUs to suspend (all CPUs but the current one). It acquires the speaker timer when acpi_resume_beep is non-zero, sets the firmware waking vector to sc->acpi_wakephys, calls intr_suspend and saves the context into the first suspend pcb with savectx. In the branch taken when savectx returns non-zero it saves the FPU state, suspends the other CPUs (printing 'Failed to suspend APs' and returning 0 if that fails), patches the wake code variables (resume beep, reset video, EFER when NX is supported, CR4, pcb pointer, GDT limit and base), remaps low memory with pmap_remap_lowptdi(true) and enters the sleep state (AcpiEnterSleepStateS4bios when state is S4 and sc->acpi_s4bios is set, otherwise AcpiEnterSleepState), printing a message and returning 0 on failure. If the sleep call returns and acpi_susp_bounce is set it calls resumectx(pcb); otherwise it spins in a pause loop waiting for the system to power down. The other branch (reached after the machine resumes through the saved context) re-initializes the console with cnresume, restores the FPU state and returns 1 (woken up successfully).
note: acpi_wakeup.c:191-270. Reviewer round 2 right (acpi_wakeaddr == 0 returns -1, 196-197 rather than being a precondition). Returns 197, 217, 251 (0), 269 (1). Not read: savectx/resumectx semantics (which branch executes when), intr_suspend.

name: bios16
prose: Calls a 16-bit BIOS entry point from i386 protected mode; returns an errno or the value returned by bios16_call. The fmt string describes the variadic arguments: 'p' (32-bit pointer, also tracks the lowest and highest pointer and sets the args flag), 'i' (32-bit integer), 'U', 'D' and 'C' (16-bit selectors for the BIOS utility, data and code segments) and 's' (16-bit integer); any other character returns EINVAL (in either pass over fmt). In the first pass it computes the stack size needed starting 32 bytes below the page end (padding the top of the stack). If a pointer argument was given and the span between the lowest and highest pointer exceeds 16 pages it returns EACCES; otherwise it sets the args segment base to the lowest pointer and limit 0xffff, sets the 32-bit code segment base from bios16_jmp, enters the BIOS pmap with pmap_bios16_enter and, in the second pass, builds the argument frame on that stack (pointers become offsets from the lowest pointer plus the args selector). It sets the BIOS selectors, loads the call vector with the entry offset and the 16-bit code selector, calls bios16_call(&args->r, stack_top), leaves the BIOS pmap and returns the call's value.
note: bios.c:319-438. Returns 370 (EINVAL), 377 (EACCES), 427 (EINVAL), 438. Not read: bios16_call, pmap_bios16_enter/leave, set_bios_selectors. The size check 375-377 appears under `if (flags & BIOSARGS_FLAG)` as shown by the filtered listing (braces not displayed), so EACCES is only possible when a 'p' argument was given.

name: bios_oem_strings
prose: Collects OEM identification strings from the BIOS ROM area into buffer; returns the string length or a negative code. It returns -1 if oem or buffer is NULL or maxlen is below 2, -2 if there is no signature list, and -3 if the search range is empty or outside the BIOS area (BIOS_START to BIOS_START + BIOS_SIZE). For each signature (anchor, offset, totlen) it returns -4 after printing a message if the offset range is outside the BIOS area, or -5 after printing a message if the string would not fit in maxlen - 1 bytes. It scans the BIOS memory for the anchor text from the start of the range up to to - len, and for the first match copies tot bytes starting at the given offset into buffer, replacing characters outside 0x20-0x7E by spaces, dropping leading spaces and collapsing runs of spaces. After all signatures it removes one trailing space (when more than one character was stored), terminates the buffer with NUL and returns idx, the number of characters stored.
note: bios.c:442-516. Returns 451, 455, 460, 475, 483, 516. The two printf paths report the signature, offsets and bounds. Not read: BIOS_PADDRTOVADDR macro.

name: initializecpu
prose: Applies CPU-specific initialization on i386 for the CPU being brought up; void. It switches on the detected cpu type: the old 486-class parts call their init routines (init_bluelightning, init_486dlc, init_cy486dx, init_5x86, init_6x86, and for a 486 on a 386 init_i486_on_386); 586-class parts depend on the vendor (AMD K5/K6 write-allocate enabling and a TSC-through-suspend MSR bit for family 0xa0, Centaur init_winchip, Transmeta init_transmeta, Rise init_rise); 686-class parts depend on the vendor (Intel init_ppro or init_mendocino for specific steppings, AMD optional SSE enabling via the HWCR MSR for some models and, for families 0xf and 0x10 without a hypervisor, setting cpu_amdc1e_bug, Centaur init_via, Transmeta init_transmeta); other types do nothing. It then, for all CPUs that have SSE and FXSR, sets CR4_FXSR | CR4_XMM and sets cpu_fxsr and hw_instruction_sse to 1; if elf32_nxstack is set it sets EFER_NXE in the EFER MSR; and if the CPU has RDTSCP or RDPID it writes MSR_TSC_AUX with cpu_auxmsr(), which asserts (KASSERT) that interrupts are disabled and returns the CPU id. Interrupts need to be disabled only for that last step (the assertion), not for the rest.
note: initcpu.c:651-781. Reviewer original right (cpu_auxmsr's interrupts-disabled requirement and the cpu_fxsr/hw_instruction_sse assignments at 770-773 were omitted); round 15 right (the interrupts-disabled requirement matters only when RDTSCP or RDPID is present, 778-780). Not read: the init_* helpers. PARTLY READ: preprocessor-conditional branches are described as compiled in.

name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, pinit0)
prose: Generated function pmap_pae_pinit0 or pmap_nopae_pinit0 (named by the __CONCAT(PMTYPE, pinit0) definition head): initializes the pmap of process 0 (statically allocated, already using the boot page directory); void. It initializes the pmap mutex (PMAP_LOCK_INIT), sets pm_pdir to IdlePTD (and, in the PAE build, pm_pdpt to IdlePDPT), initializes the page-table-page radix tree, clears pm_active, initializes the pv chunk list, zeroes pm_stats and calls pmap_activate_boot(pmap). It allocates no memory and returns nothing.

name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, pinit)
prose: Generated function pmap_pae_pinit or pmap_nopae_pinit (named by the __CONCAT(PMTYPE, pinit) head): initializes a preallocated, zeroed pmap; returns 1 on success and 0 if the page-directory kernel virtual address cannot be allocated. Only when pmap->pm_pdir is NULL it allocates NBPTD bytes of KVA for it (returning 0 if that fails), in the PAE build allocates the PDPT from pdptzone (M_WAITOK|M_ZERO, with debug assertions on alignment and 4 GB placement), and initializes the page-table-page radix tree; when pm_pdir is already set it only asserts (KASSERT) that the radix tree is empty. It then allocates the NPGPTD page-directory pages (wired, zeroed, VM_ALLOC_WAITOK, so they cannot fail), fills the PDPT entries for PAE, maps the pages at pm_pdir with pmap_qenter, in the PAE build flushes the PDPT from the cache when the CPU has no PAT, copies the TRPTDI kernel page-directory entry from PTD, clears pm_active, initializes the pv chunk list, zeroes pm_stats and returns 1.
note: pmap.c:2052-2106. Reviewer round 1 right (the PAE pm_pdpt allocation happens only when pm_pdir was NULL, 2060-2072); round 2 (pmap_release not freeing the pm_pdir KVA) not verified: pmap_release was not read, and the prose makes no claim about release.

name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, growkernel)
prose: Generated function pmap_pae_growkernel or pmap_nopae_growkernel (named by the __CONCAT(PMTYPE, growkernel) head): grows the kernel page tables so kernel virtual addresses up to addr are mapped; returns KERN_SUCCESS or KERN_RESOURCE_SHORTAGE. Precondition: the kernel map's system mutex is held (mtx_assert). It rounds addr up to a multiple of NBPDR and limits it to vm_map_max(kernel_map). While kernel_vm_end is below addr: if the page-directory entry for kernel_vm_end is already present it advances kernel_vm_end by one NBPDR (limited to the map maximum, ending the loop there) and continues; otherwise it allocates a wired, zeroed page table page (VM_ALLOC_INTERRUPT | NOFREE | WIRED | ZERO), returning KERN_RESOURCE_SHORTAGE if none is available, sets its pindex, increments nkpt, installs the new page-directory entry in the kernel page directory and in all pmaps with pmap_kenter_pde, and advances kernel_vm_end (again limited to the map maximum). It returns KERN_SUCCESS when the loop ends.

name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, protect)
prose: Generated function pmap_pae_protect or pmap_nopae_protect (head __CONCAT(PMTYPE, protect)): reduces the access permissions of the mappings in [sva, eva) of a pmap; void. With prot == VM_PROT_NONE it calls pmap_remove(pmap, sva, eva) and returns. Otherwise, in the PAE build it returns without changes when both write and execute are requested; in the non-PAE build it returns without changes when write is requested (such a request would not reduce permissions). If the pmap is not the current one it takes the global pv-list lock and pins the thread. For each page-directory range it skips absent page directory entries; for a large (PG_PS) mapping it protects it as a unit with pmap_protect_pde when the range covers the whole large page, otherwise it takes the pv lock (restarting the whole operation if it cannot be taken without blocking) and demotes the mapping, continuing if the demotion destroyed the mapping. For each valid PTE it clears PG_RW and PG_M when write is not requested (calling vm_page_dirty first for a managed, modified, writable page); in the PAE build it sets the NX bit when execute is not requested and i386_read_exec is not set; if the entry changed it stores it with an atomic compare-and-set (retrying on conflict), invalidates the page at once when it was a global mapping, and otherwise remembers that TLB entries must be flushed (flushed for the whole pmap at the end). It releases the pmap lock, unpins and releases the pv lock when it was taken.
note: pmap.c:3309-3455. Reviewer round 17 right (PAE NX is set only when execute is not requested and !i386_read_exec, 3426-3428). PARTLY READ: the tail after 3450 (unlock sequence) not displayed.

name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, enter_object)
prose: Generated function pmap_pae_enter_object or pmap_nopae_enter_object (head __CONCAT(PMTYPE, enter_object)): maps the resident pages of an object, starting at m_start, into [start, end) of a pmap with the given protection; void. Precondition: the caller holds the object's lock (asserted with VM_OBJECT_ASSERT_LOCKED on m_start->object); the lock stays held. It iterates the object's pages from m_start->pindex up to a limit of m_start->pindex + atop(end - start) (the page at the limit pindex is not included), taking the global pv-list lock and the pmap lock for the whole loop. For each page it computes va = start + ptoa(pindex - m_start->pindex); if va is large-page aligned, a whole large page fits below end, the page has psind 1 and super pages are enabled, it tries pmap_enter_4mpage: on KERN_SUCCESS or KERN_NO_SPACE it jumps NBPDR / PAGE_SIZE pages ahead in the iterator (so on KERN_NO_SPACE the skipped pages are not mapped individually); otherwise it maps the single page with pmap_enter_quick_locked, passing the previous page-table page as a hint, and steps to the next page. Only resident pages found by the iterator are mapped (holes are skipped). It then releases the pmap and global locks.
note: pmap.c:4099-4129. Reviewer round 1 right (the caller's object lock remains held), round 2 right (the iterator limit excludes the page at the end pindex), round 15 right (on KERN_NO_SPACE the iterator still jumps ahead, 4119-4121).

name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, enter_quick)
prose: Generated function pmap_pae_enter_quick or pmap_nopae_enter_quick (head __CONCAT(PMTYPE, enter_quick)): quickly maps one resident page m at va in a pmap with the given protection; void. It takes the global pv-list write lock and the pmap lock, calls pmap_enter_quick_locked(pmap, va, m, prot, NULL), ignoring its result, and releases both locks. The mapping is created only if the helper succeeds: pmap_enter_quick_locked returns NULL without mapping (and drops the page-table-page reference it took) when a large page already covers the address, when allocating a page table page fails (no sleeping), when the PTE already holds a mapping, or when a pv entry cannot be inserted for a managed page; otherwise it builds a valid, read-only (user-accessible for non-kernel pmaps) PTE, optionally sets NX in the PAE build when execute is not requested and i386_read_exec is not set, and may attempt superpage promotion.
note: pmap.c:4141-4150 and the helper 4153-4267 (the helper's behaviour is included because the outcome of this function is the helper's).

name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, kenter_temporary)
prose: Generated function pmap_pae_kenter_temporary or pmap_nopae_kenter_temporary (head __CONCAT(PMTYPE, kenter_temporary)): makes a temporary kernel mapping for a physical address, meant for crash dumps; returns the base of the crash dump map area as a void pointer (crashdumpmap, not the mapped page itself unless i is 0). It computes va = crashdumpmap + i * PAGE_SIZE, maps pa there with pmap_kenter, invalidates the TLB entry for va with invlpg and returns (void *)crashdumpmap.
note: pmap.c:4274-4282. The return value is the map base for any i, as the code returns crashdumpmap, not va.

name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, object_init_pt)
prose: Generated function pmap_pae_object_init_pt or pmap_nopae_object_init_pt (head __CONCAT(PMTYPE, object_init_pt)): pre-maps a large device or scatter-gather object region with large pages; void. Precondition: the object is write-locked and is OBJT_DEVICE or OBJT_SG (asserted). Only when super pages are enabled and both addr and size are multiples of the large page size does it do anything: it populates the object (returning if that fails), takes the first page, aborts (returns) if the first page's physical address is not large-page aligned, and aborts if any following page is not physically contiguous or has a different PAT memory mode. Otherwise it locks the pmap and, for each large page in the range, stores a PG_PS | PG_M | PG_A | PG_U | PG_RW | PG_V page directory entry when the pde is currently 0 (existing entries are left as they are), adding the page count to resident_count and counting pmap_pde_mappings, and unlocks. In every other case it does nothing.

name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, unwire)
prose: Generated function pmap_pae_unwire or pmap_nopae_unwire (head __CONCAT(PMTYPE, unwire)): clears the wired attribute on all mappings in [sva, eva); void. If the pmap is not the current one it takes the global pv-list write lock and pins the thread; it locks the pmap. For each page-directory range it skips invalid page directory entries; for a large page it panics if PG_W is not set, clears PG_W and reduces wired_count by NBPDR / PAGE_SIZE when the range covers the whole large page, otherwise it demotes the mapping (taking the pv lock with a try-lock and restarting the operation if it would block; a failed demotion panics). For each valid PTE in the range it panics if PG_W is not set and clears PG_W atomically and decrements the pmap's wired count (the clearing code follows the displayed lines). Invalid entries are ignored. No TLB invalidation is done because PG_W is not a hardware bit. It releases the locks it took.
note: pmap.c:4368-4450. PARTLY READ: the atomic clear and the unlock tail after line 4440 not displayed.

name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, set_nx)
prose: Generated function pmap_pae_set_nx or pmap_nopae_set_nx (head __CONCAT(PMTYPE, set_nx)): enables no-execute support for the PAE pmap; void. In the PAE build it returns without doing anything when the CPU has no NX capability (AMDID_NX clear in amd_feature); otherwise it sets pg_nx to PG_NX and sets elf32_nxstack to 1. In the non-PAE build the function does nothing.

name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, bootstrap)
prose: Generated function pmap_pae_bootstrap or pmap_nopae_bootstrap (head __CONCAT(PMTYPE, bootstrap)): brings the pmap module in sync with the page tables built by pmap_cold; void. It sets virtual_avail to firstaddr and virtual_end to VM_MAX_KERNEL_ADDRESS, initializes the statically allocated kernel pmap (mutex, pm_pdir = IdlePTD, pm_pdpt = IdlePDPT in PAE, pm_active set for all CPUs, resident_count from the pages used by bootstrap, pv chunk list, radix tree) and the global pv lock. It then carves reserved kernel virtual addresses and PTEs with the SYSMAP macro starting at virtual_avail: this CPU's cmap pages and qmap address, CMAP3 (boot memory test), the crash dump maps, ptvmmap, the message buffer, the KPTD/KPTmap area (filling KPTD[i] for the NKPT initial page tables), and the PMAP1, PMAP2 and PMAP3 temporary mappings, initializes the PMAP2 mutex, sets virtual_avail to the end of those reservations and calls pmap_init_pat().
note: pmap.c:607-720. PARTLY READ: macro-generated reservations read as listed; no error returns exist in the function.

name: i386_set_ldt
prose: Implements the i386_set_ldt system call to set, allocate or clear user LDT entries; returns 0 or an errno and sets td_retval[0] to the start index on success except in the clear case. If descs is NULL: for start == 0 and num == 0 it selects the whole user range (NLDT to MAX_LD); under dt_lock it returns 0 when the process has no LDT or start is beyond its length, else zeroes the descriptors in the range (clipped to the LDT length) and returns 0 without setting td_retval[0]. For descriptors supplied: unless the call is the auto-allocation request (start == LDT_AUTO_ALLOC and num == 1) it returns EINVAL if start is not below MAX_LD or start + num exceeds MAX_LD. It then checks every descriptor: SDT_SYSNULL entries have their present bit cleared in the caller-supplied descriptor (so descs is modified); system types (TSS, LDT, task and interrupt/trap/call gates) return EACCES; conforming code segment types require the present bit (EACCES otherwise); ordinary data and code types are accepted; any other type returns EINVAL; a present descriptor whose privilege level is not SEL_UPL returns EACCES. For the auto-allocation request it takes dt_lock, grows the LDT if there is none, scans from NLDT for the first free (SDT_SYSNULL) slot, growing the LDT by one entry and retrying when none is free, sets uap->start to that slot and stores the descriptor with i386_set_ldt_data; otherwise it takes dt_lock, grows the LDT to start + num and stores the descriptors. On success it sets td_retval[0] to uap->start; on error it returns the error.
note: sys_machdep.c:554-701. Reviewer original right (descs == NULL success does not set td_retval, 570-593), round 2 right (SYSNULL entries have sd_p cleared, so descs must be writable, 608-610), round 15 right (descriptors are validated: EINVAL/EACCES paths 598-657). Not read: i386_ldt_grow, i386_set_ldt_data beyond its loop head.

name: vm86_emulate
prose: Emulates one privileged instruction trapped in vm86 mode; int, returning 0, a signal number (SIGTRAP when the trap flag was set, SIGBUS when the instruction cannot be emulated, SIGKILL for a fatal STI) or the retcode. If curpcb->pcb_ext is 0 it returns SIGBUS (so pcb_ext non-zero is not a precondition). retcode starts as SIGTRAP when PSL_T is set in the frame's eflags, else 0. It fetches the opcode at cs:ip, skipping an address-size prefix; the operand-size prefix is handled separately. With the CPU's virtual-mode-extensions (vm86_has_vme): an operand-size-prefixed PUSHF pushes the flags with the virtual interrupt flag (VIF) reflected as the interrupt flag, advances ip and returns retcode; POPF pops the flags, sets or clears VIF, advances ip and returns retcode unless a virtual interrupt is pending (VIP), in which case it falls out to return SIGBUS; any other operand-size-prefixed opcode and INT n fall out to SIGBUS; STI sets VIF, advances ip and returns SIGKILL if VIP was not set (printing 'fatal sti'), else falls out to SIGBUS; POPF and IRET pop their values, update the flags and VIF and return retcode unless VIP is pending (then SIGBUS); other opcodes return SIGBUS. Without VME the emulation uses the vm86 structure's own virtual eflags: operand-size-prefixed PUSHF and POPF, CLI, STI, PUSHF, INTn (using the interrupt redirection bitmap: a set bit falls out to SIGBUS; otherwise it pushes flags, cs and the return ip, loads the vector from the real-mode table, clears TF and VIF), IRET and POPF are emulated and return retcode; STI, POPF and IRET with VIP pending fall out to SIGBUS; an operand-size-prefixed opcode other than PUSHF/POPF, and unknown opcodes, return SIGBUS.
note: vm86.c:179-386 (this record's slice is the first half; same function as the next record). Reviewer original right (pcb_ext == 0 returns SIGBUS, 193-194); round 15 wrong: an operand-size-prefixed opcode other than PUSHF/POPF does not return retcode, it breaks out of the inner switch to `return (SIGBUS)` (237, 284, 316).

name: vm86_emulate
prose: Emulates one privileged instruction trapped in vm86 mode; int, returning 0, a signal number (SIGTRAP when the trap flag was set, SIGBUS when the instruction cannot be emulated, SIGKILL for a fatal STI) or the retcode. If curpcb->pcb_ext is 0 it returns SIGBUS. retcode starts as SIGTRAP when PSL_T is set in the frame's eflags, else 0. It fetches the opcode at cs:ip, skipping an address-size prefix. With virtual-mode extensions (vm86_has_vme) it emulates operand-size-prefixed PUSHF and POPF, STI (SIGKILL when no virtual interrupt is pending, else SIGBUS), POPF and IRET, and returns SIGBUS for INT n, other prefixed opcodes and unknown opcodes, and for POPF/IRET/STI when a virtual interrupt is pending. Without VME it emulates, using the vm86 structure's virtual eflags, operand-size-prefixed PUSHF and POPF, CLI, STI, PUSHF, INT n (a set bit in the interrupt redirection map falls out to SIGBUS), IRET and POPF, each returning retcode on success and falling out to SIGBUS when VIP is pending after STI, POPF or IRET; an operand-size-prefixed opcode other than PUSHF/POPF and any unknown opcode return SIGBUS.
note: vm86.c:179-386 (second slice of the same function). Reviewer original right (pcb_ext == 0 returns SIGBUS), round 15 wrong (non-PUSHF/POPF prefixed opcodes return SIGBUS, 316, 284).
